newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - US stocks seen up on jobs report.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - US stocks seen up on jobs report.

text.p: U.S. stocks are seen higher with bonds after the October jobs report pointed to no inflationary pressures, analysts said. The following are their comments:
PHILIP ORLANDO, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER AT VALUE LINE

-- "The non-farm payrolls were about in line. But more importantly, there had been concern that September's would go from minus 40,000 to a revision of plus 100,000 and that didn't happen. There was no rise in average hourly earnings. There's no inflation out there."
Average earnings per hour were unchanged at $11.91.
-- Orlando added, "On balance this is a good report and bonds should rally on this." He sees the Dow headed for 6150 next week. The Dow on Thursday rose 36 points to 6029.
HUGH JOHNSON, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER AT FIRST ALBANY CORP:

-- "It's got a little bit of good and bad news in it. The increase in jobs of 210,000 and reduction in the prior month's decline is just to the darkside of things. At the same time average hourly earnings is good news because it's down.

-- "With the unemployment rate at 5.2 percent, this report does not show upward pressure on wages. This is a big relief for the Fed and bond market. Today we will have modestly higher bonds and stocks. But this report is not a major mover."
HILDEGARD ZAGORSKI, A MARKET ANALYST AT PRUDENTIAL SECURITIES:
-- "It's about what we were expecting. They are okay numbers. The bonds are rallying on this data, and I would suspect that stocks will follow."
Also reported was September leading indicators, up 0.1 percent. Analysts said the data were stale compared with the October jobs report.
The long bond surged 19/32, knocking its yield down to 6.60 percent, a fresh seven-month low. December S&P index futures rose 2.15 to 711.80, indicating the Dow would rise about 17 points.
